explain.say: Flour is mostly starch, packed in tight, ordered grains. In the hot oven the starch soaks up water, its grains swell, and their order breaks down, making the crumb soft.

faq.q: Is stale bread just dried out?
faq.a: Not mainly. Bread can go stale even sealed in a bag, because its starch slowly crystallises again. Losing water plays a smaller part.

faq.q: Why does bread go stale faster in the fridge?
faq.a: Starch crystallises fastest at cool fridge temperatures, so bread stales several times faster there than on the counter. Freezing stops it almost completely.
asks: Should bread go in the fridge?

faq.q: Why does toasting refresh stale bread?
faq.a: Heat melts the starch crystals again so the crumb softens, at least until it cools down and starts staling again.
asks: How do you make stale bread soft?

faq.q: Why do crackers go soft but bread goes hard?
faq.a: Crackers are very dry, so they soak up moisture from the air and go soft. Bread goes hard mainly because of its starch, not because of air.
Keep bread you will eat in a day or two in a bread bin or bag at room temperature. Freeze the rest, and toast or warm it straight from frozen.
asks: What is the best way to keep bread fresh?

facts: Bread goes stale several times faster in the fridge than at room temperature.
Warming stale bread melts its starch crystals and softens it again for a while.
